questions.q: Which table stores every catalog item a requester can browse and order?
options: sc_req_item
sc_cat_item
sc_category
sys_user
questions.explain: sc_cat_item is the catalog item table — the record behind every tile a requester clicks in the Service Catalog.

questions.q: What field on sc_category creates the parent-child relationship used for subcategories (e.g., Hardware > Laptops & Desktops)?
options: A Parent field that references another sc_category record
A Catalog field that references sc_catalog
There is no such field; subcategories require a separate table
The Order field
questions.explain: sc_category is self-referencing — its Parent field points to another category record, which is how the hierarchy is built without extra tables.

questions.q: Why would an organization configure more than one sc_catalog record?
options: It's required for every category to have an Order field
To serve genuinely different audiences, such as a separate internal employee catalog and an external customer catalog, each with its own branding and visibility
sc_cat_item requires a different catalog for every category
Multiple catalogs are required before any variables can be added
questions.explain: Most orgs run a single catalog, but the platform supports multiple catalogs for distinct audiences with different branding, visible categories, and access.

questions.q: A catalog item's Delivery time field is best described as:
options: A required field that triggers an approval workflow automatically
A field that only exists on Record Producers
A plain-language fulfillment expectation shown to the requester before they order, set by the admin based on the real SLA
A system-generated timestamp recorded after the item is ordered
questions.explain: Delivery time is set by the administrator to communicate a realistic expectation to the requester, based on the actual fulfillment process behind the item.

questions.q: What is the real-world path a requester follows to reach and order a catalog item?
options: Catalog item first, then category, then catalog
Catalog (sc_catalog) → category hierarchy (sc_category) → catalog item (sc_cat_item) → Order Now
Category first, then variable set, then approval
There is no fixed order; all three tables are interchangeable entry points
questions.explain: A requester opens a catalog, browses through one or more nested categories, and lands on the specific item before ordering it.
